g.data-frame: 07A Observability and alerting: signals to response

rect.data-title: 07A Observability and alerting: signals to response

g.textArea: 07A Observability and alerting: signals to response
CTO / developers / QA / DevOps | Draft | Use relevant signals to detect impact, notify an accountable responder and verify recovery.
Blue = proposed | Gray = reported context or reference | Yellow = exception, boundary or team decision
Reported context and the requested improvement

rect.data-content:
Observability tools are reported as deployed
The Nov 12 discussion questioned their effective use and the visibility of alerts.
Current coverage and configuration still need verification.

Explicit request: enable alerting for the team
Turn useful symptoms into actionable notifications.
Route by service, environment and severity to a responsible role.
Agree backup and escalation coverage.

Start by checking the complete path
Inventory tools, instrumentation, rules and destinations.
Check whether notifications reach the intended people.
Record detection and response gaps with owners.

g.textArea: Proposed: an observable service and an accountable response path

rect.data-content:
1. Workload and dependencies
Apps, infrastructure and data services.
Critical journeys and availability probes.
Identify product, environment and version.

2. Relevant telemetry
Availability, errors, latency and capacity.
Metrics/logs; traces where useful.
Include environment and instance context.

3. Ingest, store and query
Dashboards and investigation links.
Check collection health and freshness.
Actual tools and coverage: verify first.

4. Evaluate useful alert rules
Agree thresholds and time windows.
Define missing-data behavior.
Severity and routing match the impact.

5. Deliver a useful notification
Named destination and primary/backup.
Include impact, scope and runbook link.
Channels and recipients: team decision.

6. Acknowledge and respond
Assign incident ownership; investigate.
Mitigate and verify service recovery.
Record outcome and follow-up actions.

Developers and QA also inspect signals directly
Developers correlate failures with service/release context. QA observes test behavior and saves evidence tied to the manifest and instance.
Alerting complements investigation; a missing signal must have an explicit policy.

g.textArea: Expected outcomes
Coverage to agree
Decisions for the team

rect.data-content:
• Detect meaningful impact and collection gaps.
• Give developers/QA usable investigation evidence.
• Reach an accountable responder with useful context.
• Verify recovery and improve noisy or missing rules.

• Critical services, dependencies and user journeys.
• Availability, errors, latency and resource saturation.
• Telemetry/notification delivery health.
• Product, environment, release and instance labels.

• Tools, instrumentation and useful service targets.
• Rule thresholds, windows, severity and no-data policy.
• Destinations, primary/backup and response coverage.
• Escalation, retention, access and review cadence.

Match alerting to the environment purpose
Temporary QA needs test/instance context and expected expiry/cleanup handling. Customer demos, client pilots and production need agreed stable-service monitoring and support coverage.
Use 05B environment lifecycle to scope QA behavior and 06B documentation maintenance for owned runbooks. Test alerts and maintenance silences need a clear scope and end.

g.textArea: Basis: proposal notes and Nov 12 discussion (05:56–06:42). Current gaps are reported concerns; actual tools, live rules, channels, recipients and response arrangements remain to verify.

g.data-frame: 07B Observability: detect, notify, respond and verify recovery

rect.data-title: 07B Observability: detect, notify, respond and verify recovery

g.textArea: 07B Observability: detect, notify, respond and verify recovery
Workloads / observability operators / responders / developers / QA | Draft | Prove the full notification and response path, including failures and missing acknowledgements.
Blue = proposed | Gray = reported context or reference | Yellow = exception, boundary or team decision
Workloads / signals
Detection / routing
Responders / investigation
Mitigation / recovery
Closure / improvement

rect.data-content:
1. Produce signals [Workload / probe]
Emit selected service/dependency telemetry.
Tag product, environment, release and instance.
Include probe results for agreed user journeys.

Missing or stale telemetry
Evaluate the agreed absence/staleness window.
Distinguish expected QA expiry from failure.
Route actionable loss of visibility via Step 4.

Notification delivery fails
Record the failed route and use the agreed alternate destination.
Assign an owner to restore the notification path.
Validate delivery again; do not treat a sent event as receipt.

2. Collect and check [Observability]
Ingest/store/query the relevant signals.
Check collection health and freshness.
Preserve context for dashboards and evidence.

3. Evaluate rule [Alerting system]
Apply agreed condition, window and severity.
Group duplicates and check scoped silences.
If no condition fires, continue observation.

4. Notify the responsible role [Routing]
Select service/environment primary and backup coverage.
Send scope, symptom, severity, evidence and runbook link.
Check channel delivery and start the agreed acknowledgement timer.

No acknowledgement within agreed time
Escalate to the designated backup/support role.
Confirm someone accepts incident ownership.
Coverage and escalation timing remain to agree.

5. Acknowledge [Primary / backup]
Confirm receipt and name the incident owner.
Assess impact and start the incident record.
Escalate if coverage or expertise is insufficient.

6. Investigate [Responder + service owner]
Correlate dashboards/logs/traces with the affected version.
Use the runbook; involve developers or QA as relevant.
Separate product, environment and telemetry failures.

Mitigation fails or impact stays unclear
Keep the incident open and reassess Step 6.
Escalate to the appropriate service owner.
Record failed actions and the next decision.

7. Mitigate [Authorized operator]
Choose a scoped action using the runbook.
Use existing change/access controls.
Record the action, owner and observed result.

8. Verify recovery [Responder / QA as needed]
Check the affected service/journey and fresh telemetry.
Confirm recovery against agreed conditions, not only alert status.
If still unhealthy, return to Step 6; keep incident ownership.

Keep an operating record and control expected noise
Record environment/instance, impact, timeline, acknowledgement, actions and recovery evidence.
Scope test/maintenance silences and their expiry; align temporary QA rules with the environment lifecycle.
Review notification-path health and stale collection separately from workload health.

9. Close and improve [Incident / service owner]
Communicate recovery through the agreed incident process.
Retain evidence and assign unresolved follow-up work.
Tune missing/noisy rules and update the owned runbook.
Repeat validation after rule, route or ownership changes.

g.textArea: Proposed operating flow. Tool capabilities, alert conditions, notification channels, acknowledgement tracking, incident process and response coverage require team agreement and testing.

g.data-frame: 07C Observability and alerting: delivery plan and controls

rect.data-title: 07C Observability and alerting: delivery plan and controls

g.textArea: 07C Observability and alerting: delivery plan and controls
DevOps / service owners / developers / QA | Draft | Verify existing coverage, agree actionable rules, then test delivery, response and recovery before expanding.
Blue = proposed | Gray = reported context or reference | Yellow = exception, boundary or team decision
Proposed work packages

rect.data-content:
1. Verify the existing setup
Inventory tools, signals, dashboards and rules.
Map services, dependencies and environments.
Check destinations and current ownership.
Prioritize gaps around critical user impact.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: DevOps + service owners

rect.data-content:
2. Agree alerts and response coverage
Define symptoms, severity and rule windows.
Choose thresholds and missing-data behavior.
Name primary/backup roles and destinations.
Agree acknowledgement and escalation timing.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: Service owners + DevOps + support leads

rect.data-content:
3. Configure a focused first scope
Complete required instrumentation and labels.
Connect dashboards, rules and notification routes.
Prepare runbooks and incident records.
Include telemetry and delivery-path health.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: DevOps + developers + service owners

rect.data-content:
4. Exercise, tune and expand
Test controlled impact and absent/stale data.
Prove delivery, acknowledgement and escalation.
Verify recovery, noise handling and QA expiry.
Expand coverage and assign recurring review.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: QA + responders + DevOps
Acceptance evidence before expansion
Inputs and coordination
Operating controls to agree
Open decisions for review

rect.data-content:
• Controlled failure creates the expected scoped alert and context.
• Actual primary receives it; acknowledgement/ownership is recorded.
• Failed delivery and no acknowledgement exercise alternate/escalation paths.
• Fresh signals and the affected journey confirm recovery.
• Missing data, duplicate noise, silences and temporary QA expiry are tested.

• Verified tool configuration and access to relevant telemetry.
• Critical-service inventory, labels and agreed impact targets.
• Supported notification destinations and response arrangements.
• Approved test scenarios and environment/release context from 05.
• Owned runbooks and maintenance workflow from 06.

• Version/review rule and routing changes; retain test evidence.
• Primary/backup ownership, escalation and support coverage.
• Grouping, scoped silence expiry and periodic noise/coverage review.
• Data minimization/redaction, access, retention and collection cost.
• Observe the telemetry and notification paths as well as workloads.

• Which tools, services, journeys and signals are in the first scope?
• Which impact targets, thresholds, windows and no-data rules apply?
• Which channels, responding roles, hours and escalation timings?
• How do QA, demo, pilot and production policies differ?
• Who owns rule/runbook changes, retention, cost and recurring tests?

Completion means the alert reaches an accountable responder and recovery is verified
A deployed dashboard or a configured rule alone does not demonstrate the full operating path. Capture evidence from signal through receipt, response and recovery.
Validate and extend the existing setup first. Tool replacement, numeric service targets, 24/7 coverage, named recipients and implementation dates are decisions, not commitments.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 request to enable alerting. This is a proposed delivery approach; current tools, coverage, rules, routes and operating ownership have not been re-audited here.
